item.title: Assembly Drill 2026-11-10: reverse-function
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64.
Reverse this short function to equivalent C:
```asm mystery: mov eax, ecx cdq xor eax, edx sub eax, edx ret ```
What does it return for 5, -5, 0 and -2147483647?
---
## Answer
```c int mystery(int x) { return x < 0 ? -x : x; // branchless abs() } ```
Results: 5, 5, 0, 2147483647.
## Explanation
- `cdq` (opcode 99) sign-extends eax into edx: edx = 0 for x >= 0, or 0xFFFFFFFF (-1) for x < 0, i.e. the sign mask. - For negative x, `xor` with -1 gives ~x and `sub` of -1 adds 1, so ~x + 1 = -x (two's-complement negate). For non-negative x both steps do nothing. - No branch is needed. INT_MIN (0x80000000) stays negative, since +2^31 doesn't fit in an int.
